significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) double dissociation—"reversing only the order of two events" changes prognosis signals for directed progression pairs but not order-invariant comorbidities—combined with the form-(ii) result that steering a "progression-direction" axis causally shifts risk predictions. This fixes expected responses for a class of counterfactual trajectories rather than merely showing order is decodable, and bears directly on the temporal representations used by sequential EHR models such as BEHRT (Li et al., Scientific Reports, 2020) and the time-to-event foundation model MOTOR (Steinberg et al., 2023). It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and an internal causal mechanism; verified false would determinately rule out this selective reversal-and-steering account, although it would not prove that every possible distributed representation is symmetric co-occurrence. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit here: a generic claim that scientific mechanisms are represented would not supply the specific directed-versus-comorbidity invariance law that supports this score.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are explicitly named as the "Directionality-Beyond-Co-occurrence Index," "Reversal-vs-Comorbidity Causal Asymmetry," and the conclusion that "temporal-reversal robustness becomes a model-selection and auditing criterion." That auditing criterion is ex ante because EHR-model developers and auditors can apply it while selecting or gating a risk model before deployment, rather than only explaining an already observed error. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction remains that reversal responses will be larger and prognosis-consistent for directed pairs while remaining stable for comorbid pairs, so a relation—not merely a search procedure—can transfer across the asserted class of ordered EHR foundation models, though not automatically to other modalities or scientific domains. The topic-substitution check supports an above-median score: removing the reversal asymmetry and its named audit criterion leaves only generic representation probing, which would not provide this pre-deployment handle to auditors and EHR-model developers.
